metadata.title: How Does Claude Build an Accrual Schedule?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude decides, using its own accounting judgment, which expenses and revenues to accrue at period end -- or is doing something narrower. Lands the carry-out that a drafted accrual JE is a computed entry tied to cited support, waiting for a controller's approval, not Claude's judgment about what you owe.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet's narration carries real skill-specific facts (not unfilled template placeholders) -- see QUESTION.md. Facts preserved: the accrual-schedule skill builds the period-end accrual schedule; for each accrual it computes the entry, cites the support, and drafts the JE; used during month-end close; the JE is a draft for controller approval, not a posting. Register re-registered Teardown -> Plain; source's B03 design-tell verdict became a plain mechanism + both-directions beat; a wrong-guess beat and an anchor (a December utility bill: identified -> computed -> cited -> drafted -> stopped, waiting) were added per hai-simple's Phase 1 structure, since the source's Teardown shape carried neither.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether Claude decides which expenses to accrue using its own accounting judgment. It doesn't. Liam is here to take you through what the skill actually does, step by step.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'What decides an accrual -- judgment?', hesitates on 'judgment', corrects to 'the support', lands the real question

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('judgment' -> 'the support') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that Claude decides, using its own accounting judgment, which expenses and revenues belong in this period's accrual schedule. But the skill doesn't work that way. For each accrual, it computes the entry and cites the support that backs it. Give it an expense with no supporting document, and it won't invent a number -- there's nothing for it to cite, so there's nothing to draft.

shot.new_visual_element: An accountant-judgment figure weighing what to accrue, struck through; a written compute/cite/draft procedure lit instead

production_viz.label: Judgment, struck -- compute/cite/draft, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a figure icon labelled 'ACCOUNTING JUDGMENT' beside a thought-bubble of scattered decision marks. Right: a numbered card labelled 'COMPUTE / CITE / DRAFT'. The judgment side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the procedure side stays lit. A final line reads 'no document -- not on the list' and the figure does not reach for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: for each accrual, it computes the entry, cites the support document behind it, and drafts the journal entry -- nothing more. Watch the anchor: a December utility bill that won't be billed until January. It's identified, the entry is computed, the utility contract is cited as support, and a draft JE is created. Then it stops, waiting.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a December utility bill traveling identified -> computed -> cited -> drafted, then stopping

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one accrual, four stops
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'IDENTIFIED', 'ENTRY COMPUTED', 'SUPPORT CITED', 'JE DRAFTED'. A single highlighted token 'DEC. UTILITY BILL' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives. At the bottom, the token halts beside a label 'awaiting approval' -- it does not continue past the drafted card. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: That draft is built -- computed, cited, ready to review. But a drafted JE with a citation isn't the same as a correct entry: it only reflects what the cited document says, and a wrong document produces a wrong entry, cited correctly. And an accrual with no draft this period doesn't mean something broke -- it can mean that expense has no qualifying support yet. Either way, the draft still waits for a controller before anything posts.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, drafted and waiting; splits into 'cited is not correct' and 'no draft is not broken'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- drafted, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'JE DRAFTED' card beside 'awaiting approval'. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'CITED: OK' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'CORRECT?' beneath it, labelled 'cited is not correct'; right reads 'NO DRAFT' beside a faint 'no support yet' note, labelled 'no draft is not broken'.

beats.narration_text: A drafted accrual JE isn't Claude's judgment about what you owe -- it's a computed entry, tied to cited support, waiting for a controller's approval before anything posts.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. Give Claude one expense that belongs in this period's close, with the invoice or contract as its support, and ask it to run the accrual-schedule skill: compute the entry, cite that document, and draft the JE. Then remove the supporting document and ask it to try the same accrual again, and watch what it does when there's nothing left to cite. Liam, in for Bear.
